pages.name: The Pyramid and the Circles of Mystery

text.content:
Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} organizes itself as a pyramid of rank: seven councilors beneath the mythical, unseen @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} himself, each overseeing a portion of the world; seven pontifices beneath each councilor, arranging matters within a continent; seven lords beneath each pontifex, overseeing a region; and seven regents beneath each lord, each commanding a chantry of apprentices. In practice the pyramid is rarely full — most cities can't support seven vampires at any given rank, let alone seven times seven — and vacancies are simply covered by collaboration, one-upmanship, or a single overworked Tremere wearing several hats at once.

Each rank additionally carries seven circles of mystery, denoting a member's depth of occult understanding and personal responsibility independent of (though often correlated with) actual authority. A fifth-circle apprentice with a well-placed lineage may outrank a brilliant but politically inert third-circle apprentice in prestige, even though the latter is the superior thaumaturge. Advancement through the ranks and circles is less a matter of law than of reward: elders dole out promotions, secrets, and political support to those who serve the clan's interests (or at least appear to), and withhold them from those who don't. Kindred outside the clan rarely grasp the structure at all, since real influence often has little to do with the titles involved.

Astors function as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} clan's secret police, tracing their authority back to the mortal days of the order and rumored to answer to a pontifex who counts himself among their number. Trained in Thaumaturgy, interrogation, investigation, and enough combat skill to finish the job, an astor's mandate is to root out treachery, stop leaks of clan secrets, and destroy any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} whose personal ambitions threaten the clan as a whole. A tribunal's declaration that a Tremere is rogue or a threat is, in practice, a death warrant carried out by the astors.

Few Tremere ever learn the identities of the dozen or so vampires who serve as astors at any given time, and the position sees high turnover — an astor tasked with executing a treacherous regent may himself run afoul of a prince's Tradition of Destruction in the process. Astors reportedly maintain a private cache of specialized rituals to occlude communications, recognize one another, and track evidence, though whether these are shared clan secrets or the personal work of individual astor-thaumaturges is unknown even within the pyramid.

Beneath the formal pyramid, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} organize into houses — informal colleges of magical or philosophical practice that persist only as long as they serve some purpose. House @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, upholding Hermetic blood magic as clan orthodoxy, claims every childe of the clan by default, but numerous smaller houses cultivate their own specialties: House Trismegistus pursues symbology and numerology; House Hashem studies Kabbalah; House Rodolfo practices divination; the Daughters of the Crone work birth and death magic; the Horned Society explores voudoun and necromancy and permits non-Kindred members; the High Saturday Auram Guild studies alchemy and likewise admits non-Tremere; and House Goratrix, the infernalist house founded by the traitor Goratrix, now exists chiefly as the Tremere antitribu of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}.

Some houses, like the social league House Massimo (which trades rituals among Italian Tremere) or House ab Flaidd (which studies Wicca as an adjunct to Hermetic Thaumaturgy), exist purely for mutual benefit and carry little stigma. Others, particularly those associated with infernalism or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} sympathies, are treated as dangerous liabilities. Storytellers and players are explicitly encouraged to invent new houses of their own to suit a chronicle's needs.

pages.name: Secret Societies: The Elite, the Children of the Pyramid, and the Guardians

text.content:
The Elite hold that Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} represents a new and superior step in vampiric existence, destined to triumph over every other clan in the Jyhad. Formed in the late 18th century, its members work quietly — a murdered rival here, a discredited enemy there, a patsy indebted through Thaumaturgy elsewhere — to advance @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} supremacy, and its more radical fringe reportedly hunts and kills non-Tremere thaumaturges to preserve the clan's monopoly on blood magic, sometimes using specialized rituals to do so. Mainstream Tremere regard the Elite as, at best, an embarrassing extremist fringe and, at worst, a bigoted gang, though elders privately tolerate its usefulness in eliminating inconvenient rivals.

Children of the Pyramid venerate the pyramid itself as the material authority of a godlike entity, with the founder Tremere cast as an unliving Son of the Pyramid. They meet in secret to discuss spiritual advancement alongside clan business, drawing heavily on the allegorical tome The Travels of Fedoso, and are prone to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.9e49e2b00b8442e3]{Hierarchical Sociology Disorder} derangement. Their fanatical loyalty makes them useful tools for a superior, if tiresome company for anyone less devout.

The Guardians of Tradition are an extreme faction of traditionalists who reject nearly all modern technology and thaumaturgical innovation, preferring candlelight, quill pens, and centuries-proven methods. Increasingly marginalized in the modern nights — a Tremere who won't use a telephone is a serious liability — the Guardians nonetheless retain real personal power through sheer age and stubbornness, and some of their most reactionary members still cling to outmoded notions of racial or theological superiority even as the rest of the clan has moved past such things.

pages.name: Defunct Orders: The Naturists, the Humanus League, and the Golden Path of Harmony

text.content:
Not every @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} secret society survives to the modern nights. The Order of Naturists grew from early ties between Eastern European @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} and Druidic and pagan traditions, including the Lithuanian Telyavs, a cult that Embraced from nature-worshipping mortals and flourished until the 1600s. The order quietly dwindled over the centuries and vanished entirely by the turn of the 20th century, alongside the utter destruction of the Telyavs themselves.

The Humanus League comprised Tremere who sought to reclaim their lost mortality, inspired by legends of the Comte St. Germain and rumors of Golconda, and who cultivated charity and compassion as a means toward that end. The relentless backstabbing of the Tremere pyramid proved incompatible with maintaining such ideals; the League collapsed under its own internal squabbling within the past decade, its survivors abandoning the cause, sinking into torpor, or being sternly reabsorbed into the clan.

The Golden @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.e763657e5a404aff]{Path of Harmony} sought to foster genuine trust and cooperation among Tremere as a bulwark against the clan's endemic treachery, but its members' willingness to turn the other cheek after every betrayal only invited further betrayal. One member became the simultaneous target of accusations of diablerie, infernalism, fratricide, and giving offense to an elder from four separate sources — a fate emblematic of how poorly trusting souls fare among the Tremere.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Tremere, Chapter Two: Inside the Pyramid
